name: drop_in_place
documentation:
Executes the destructor (if any) of the pointed-to value.

 See [`ptr::drop_in_place`] for safety concerns and examples.

 [`ptr::drop_in_place`]: crate::ptr::drop_in_place()
rules: For safety, self must be valid for reads.
For safety, self must be valid for writes.
For safety, self must be properly aligned, even if T has size 0.
For safety, self must be nonnull, even if T has size 0.
For safety, the value pointed to by self must be valid for dropping, including any additional type-specific invariants; for example, when dropping a Box, the Box's pointer to the heap must be valid.
While drop_in_place is executing, parts of the value pointed to by self may be accessed only through the &mut self references supplied to the Drop::drop methods invoked by drop_in_place.

If T is not Copy, using the pointed-to value after calling drop_in_place can cause undefined behavior. Assigning through *self counts as a use because it drops the value again; ptr::write may instead overwrite the data without dropping it.
drop_in_place may be used to drop pinned data when T is not repr(packed); pinned data must not be moved before it is dropped.
